chapter_note: This chapter is a homiletic discourse in which Mani identifies himself with the sun and his elect with its rays. The sun-imagery is used as SIMILE, not correspondence — the second side of the mapping reaches into the editorial present (Mani's mission, the elect, the gathering-up of his disciples). There is no systematic cosmos→cosmos mapping. The voice is throughout first-person Mani speaking pastorally to his community. No substratic teaching is preserved here; the chapter is editorial through and through. The sun-description in segments 5-8 is phenomenological narration in service of the simile, not impersonal cosmological mapping.
